comment: Hand-written. Families V01-V36 of docs/VANILLA_COMPLETION.md, their named mechanics, and the rules that assign every enumerated resource to a family. Statuses describe the source at the commit that changes this file; tools/compat_ledger.py validates it and generates compatibility/ledger.json and docs/VANILLA_LEDGER.md.

mechanics.name: Exact version manifests verified against the official artifacts
mechanics.note: compatibility/versions/; values read from the official jars, whose hashes match Mojang's published metadata

mechanics.name: Machine-readable feature and evidence ledger with validation
Reference traces of block state changes (circuit-trace v1)
Trace format with entity, lifecycle, inventory, dimension, ticket and RNG observations
mechanics.note: circuit-trace 2: Circuit records and evaluates it; the reference harness does not record it yet

mechanics.name: Reference harness recording v2 observations on both releases, with repeat runs
mechanics.note: Both releases; repeat runs on fresh worlds; the level random is seeded with 0

mechanics.name: Scenario adapters for official server, sequential, parallel and real-client runs with first-mismatch reports
mechanics.note: tools/scenario.py runs a skeleton sequentially, in parallel and on each harness, and reports the first difference of every pair (circuit-server --diff-fixtures)
deviations: real-client checks are separate scripts, not driven from skeletons

mechanics.name: Protocol-client scenarios compared between the official servers and Circuit
mechanics.note: External mineflayer scripts; outputs compared by diff

mechanics.name: Real-client step scripts against Circuit
mechanics.note: Checks Circuit with the unmodified client; not a comparison with the official server

mechanics.name: Internal representation of every block and state property
mechanics.note: circuit-blocks-1 from public data: 1,106 internal blocks and 27,958 internal states with stable ids; every state of both releases round-trips through notation and wire ids

mechanics.name: Per-version mapping between internal states and protocol state ids
mechanics.note: Every state of both releases maps to one Circuit state and back

mechanics.name: Collision shapes of block states
mechanics.note: Every state's collision boxes, from the block registry (minecraft-data), equal to both official servers' report; items and players move against them. Offsets some blocks apply by position are not modeled
deviations: position-dependent offsets (bamboo, pointed dripstone and others) are not applied

mechanics.name: Hardness, blast resistance, harvest tools, light emission and opacity, friction, sounds
mechanics.note: Hardness, effective tool and harvest tier of every block from public data, the tool and tier from the block tags when the official data pack is loaded; opacity from its light filtering

families.name: Item and entity components and registries

mechanics.name: Item stacks with count, stack size and damage
Other item components: names, lore, enchantments, attributes, potions, food, containers, books, maps, dyes, fireworks, trims and the rest
mechanics.note: Every component type of both protocols is read, checked against its registries and kept losslessly in canonical form (schema compiled from minecraft-data); 29 components have a save form for Anvil interchange
deviations: components that refer to registries the server does not synchronize (enchantments, trim materials and patterns, banner patterns, instruments, jukebox songs, data component predicates) are refused
the rules use only damage, max stack size and max damage

mechanics.name: Component and entity-data schema changes of 1.21.5
mechanics.note: The 1.21.5 component schema (96 types, length-prefixed creative values) is read and written
deviations: entity-data schema changes are not modeled

mechanics.name: Hashed item stacks in container clicks (1.21.5 and later)
Entity data and components (variants, custom names, equipment)
Known-pack exchange and registry data by name
mechanics.note: Vanilla pack only

mechanics.name: Synchronized registries with data for clients without the vanilla pack
mechanics.note: Each bundle names its registry set: 17 registries for 1.21.8 and 11 for 1.21.4 sent by name to clients with the vanilla pack, the same entries as the official servers; clients without the pack get a documented minimal set with data
deviations: 1.21.8 dialogs and game-test registries are not sent
clients without the vanilla pack get only dimension types, plains and the chat type with data
enchantments are sent only with the official jar's data pack

mechanics.name: Tag synchronization and evaluation
mechanics.note: With the official jar's data pack: every tag of block, item, entity type, fluid and the synchronized registries, as many per registry as the official servers send; without it, the biome tags 1.21.4 needs
deviations: tags of game events, points of interest and 1.21.8 dialogs are not loaded
tags are not reloaded while the server runs

mechanics.name: Data-pack stack, selection, ordering and reload
mechanics.note: The official jar's built-in pack, then directories and archives in configured order; later files replace earlier ones, tag files merge; pack formats checked
deviations: no pack selection, filters, overlays or /reload
the experimental packs inside the jar are not loaded

mechanics.name: Experimental feature flags and built-in experimental packs
mechanics.note: minecart_improvements, redstone_experiments, trade_rebalance in both releases

mechanics.name: The overworld dimension
mechanics.note: Flat floor, plains

mechanics.name: The Nether, the End and custom dimensions with dimension-scoped state
mechanics.note: Every level keeps its own columns, scheduled ticks, block events, block entities, entities and per-level counters, and levels tick in the order overworld, Nether, End (minecraft.wiki "Tick"); entity ids are counted over all levels. Commands, tickets, traces, checkpoints, replays and logs name the level. Differential tests prove identical coordinates in two levels independent in the engine and the oracle
deviations: the Nether and the End are neither generated nor reachable by players
level-specific rules (ultrawarm water and lava, the Nether's roof, the End's void and dragon fight) are not modeled
custom dimensions from data packs are not supported

mechanics.name: Vanilla ticket types (player, forced, portal, spawn, post-teleport and others)
mechanics.note: Typed tickets with a level, a square radius and a lifetime (minecraft.wiki "Chunk"). The server adds the start ticket (level 32 - spawnChunkRadius, none at 0; it follows /gamerule) and, per player, a loading ticket over the view distance (level 31) and a simulation ticket (level 31 - simulation distance), as observed on both official servers; /forceload adds forced tickets (level 31), which persist
deviations: post-teleport, portal, ender pearl and dragon tickets have their types and levels but nothing creates them yet

mechanics.name: Ticket level propagation and entity-ticking versus block-ticking chunks
mechanics.note: Load and simulation levels: 31 and lower entity ticking, 32 block ticking, 33 border. Scheduled ticks, block events and block entities run at simulation level 32 and lower, entities at 31 and lower; a level without players or forced chunks stops its entities and block entities after 300 ticks. Ticket changes take effect in each level's chunk stage, after its scheduled ticks
deviations: new chunks load at once; the official servers take 2 to 4 ticks, varying between runs
entity ticking per ring is observed but not compared, because item physics differ (V07, C3)

mechanics.name: Unload and reload of chunks with pending ticks, block events and entities
mechanics.note: A dropped chunk's pending ticks keep their remaining delay, counted from the tick after it dropped; after a reload its scheduled ticks and block entities run again two ticks later and its block events at once (both official servers)
deviations: the official servers may keep a dropped chunk at border for one or two ticks and restore a cached chunk during the command or in the chunk stage, which moves restored ticks by a tick between runs; Circuit drops chunks at once and restores them in the chunk stage
entities of unloaded chunks are not reported as unloaded

mechanics.name: View distance and simulation distance
mechanics.note: Per player, a loading ticket of level 31 over the view distance (two rings beyond it loaded but not simulated) and a simulation ticket of level 31 - simulation distance; chunks loaded only by the view simulate nothing, as both official servers showed (ticking.js)
deviations: the view is not compared tick by tick with the official servers, whose chunk loading timing varies

mechanics.name: Sky light propagation
mechanics.note: Sky light from above the world, undiminished straight down through cells that dampen nothing, otherwise spreading like block light; computed from the blocks at the end of the previous tick

mechanics.name: Block light emission and propagation
mechanics.note: Emission, dampening and occlusion shape of every state of both versions match the official servers; light spreads one level per block, more through dampening blocks, never through faces that occlusion shapes close together
deviations: light at the edge of the loaded area is not compared

mechanics.name: Heightmaps
mechanics.note: The heightmaps clients get are computed from the blocks: WORLD_SURFACE, MOTION_BLOCKING (states that are solid or hold a fluid, minecraft.wiki "Heightmap") and, for 1.21.8, MOTION_BLOCKING_NO_LEAVES; which states count matches both official servers for every state
deviations: server-side heightmaps (OCEAN_FLOOR and the world-generation ones) are not kept; generation and mob spawning need them (C7, C8)

mechanics.name: Day-night cycle and time advancement
mechanics.note: The world's day time advances after each tick's commands while doDaylightCycle is on, persists and goes through Anvil import and export; /time sets and queries it with the official parser and replies; set_time goes to players on joining, every 20 ticks and on changes, as on both official servers
deviations: sleeping and the other behavior that depends on the time of day, except daylight detectors, is not modeled

mechanics.name: Rain, thunder, snow and their effects
mechanics.note: Rain and thunder flags with their timers and the clear timer, advanced while doWeatherCycle is on; rain and thunder levels fading by 0.01 a tick in single precision; /weather with the official parser and replies; the client events as both official servers send them, on joining too; saved in checkpoints and carried through Anvil (minecraft.wiki "Weather", "Commands/weather")
deviations: durations are drawn from Circuit's own stream, not the level's random sequence: the same ranges, other values
snow and ice, filling cauldrons, extinguishing fire, wet farmland and other effects of rain are not modeled; sleeping does not end the weather

mechanics.name: Lightning strikes and lightning rods
mechanics.note: Lightning is an entity: it follows the entity types of C3, then thunderstorms strike

mechanics.name: Block-event FIFO
mechanics.note: One FIFO per level with set semantics: events queued by commands, scheduled ticks and block entities run in queue order (those of the entity and block-entity phases in the next tick), an equal event is queued once, an event runs only if its block is still there, and events queued while events run join the queue; events of chunks that do not tick blocks wait, keeping their place, until they do

mechanics.name: Neighbor and shape update order and the chain limit
Entity tick order
deviations: ascending id, compared with the target versions for item entities only

mechanics.name: The level random source and its draw order
deviations: only block drops, container scatter and piston sounds draw from it; random ticks and weather durations use Circuit's own derived streams, and other draws of the target versions are not made yet
mechanics.note: Each level's java.util.Random-compatible sequence, its state saved with the world; fixtures seed it with 0 as the harness does and compare raw draw counts per stage

mechanics.name: Random-tick chunk order and positions
mechanics.note: Random ticks run at simulation level 31 and lower in 1.21.8, and at 32 and lower within 128 blocks of a non-spectator player in 1.21.4
deviations: chunks in coordinate order instead of the shuffled order

mechanics.name: Biome allocation
mechanics.note: Every column is plains

mechanics.name: World presets (default, flat, large biomes, amplified, single biome, debug)
mechanics.note: A one-layer stone floor only

mechanics.name: Placed features: ores, trees, vegetation, lakes, geodes and others
Nether portal creation, search, scaling and arrival
End portals, strongholds and End gateways
Beds, respawn anchors and spawn points
deviations: respawn at the exact world spawn; the target version picks a random position around it

mechanics.name: Placement orientation and shapes: stairs, slabs, walls, fences, panes, doors, beds
deviations: only full cubes without properties, soul sand and mud, pillars, stairs, slabs, fences, panes, bars, walls, blocks facing the player, the clicked face or back along the view, rods, torches, lanterns, ladders, carpets, flowers, saplings, tall flowers, signs, banners, heads, beds and the blocks with block entities that use these rules (furnaces, smokers, blast furnaces, lecterns, beehives, ender chests, chiseled bookshelves, shulker boxes, barrels, beacons, jukeboxes, brewing stands, enchanting tables) are placed from their items besides the blocks with rules of their own; hanging signs and other blocks are not
spawners, sponges and test instance blocks are not placed
mechanics.note: Pillars along the clicked face's axis, stairs facing the player and in the clicked half, slabs in the clicked half and doubled, facing blocks toward the player or out of the clicked face, connectors and stairs with their neighbors' shapes, waterlogged in water sources, as both official servers do; every placed state checked against a report of every block item

mechanics.name: Fences, panes, bars and walls joining their neighbors
deviations: water does not flow out of waterlogged ones
mechanics.note: On shape updates and when a piston sets them down, as both official servers do; every state beside and above them compared

mechanics.name: Stairs taking corner shapes from the stairs beside them
deviations: water does not flow out of waterlogged ones
mechanics.note: On shape updates from the sides and when a piston sets them down, as both official servers do; every combination of stairs around them compared

mechanics.name: Torches, lanterns, ladders, carpets, flowers, saplings, signs and banners on their supports
deviations: flowers and saplings do not grow or spread (no random ticks for them)

other plants (grass, ferns, roots, fungi, wither roses, azaleas, tall and double plants, dripleaves, berry bushes, petals) and other attached blocks (signs, banners, vines, lichen, amethyst) are not modeled
a torch whose clicked side and floor both fail is not placed (the official servers also try the player's other looking directions)
mechanics.note: Placed by players where supported, and broken with their drops when the support goes (torches, lanterns, ladders, signs and banners on updates from their support's side, carpets, flowers and saplings on any update), as both official servers do; signs and banners stand and hang on solid blocks

mechanics.name: Two-part blocks: doors, beds, tall plants
deviations: tall grass, large ferns and other tall plants are not modeled
mechanics.note: Doors: the halves follow each other, a half without the other breaks (the lower one with the drop), and placed doors take their hinges as both official servers do; sunflowers, lilacs, rose bushes and peonies: placed with both halves, the lower one on soil, and both gone when either half or the soil goes (the lower one with the drop); beds: placed with both halves, the foot facing the player's way, a half leaving with the other, only the head dropping the bed

mechanics.name: Signs, banners, heads, pots and other block-entity data
mechanics.note: Block entities of blocks without rules of their own keep their saved data through checkpoints and Anvil interchange; one a player places starts empty and is written out as the official defaults of its type (every block's checked); nothing interprets the data, and clients do not receive it

mechanics.name: Water flow, sources and washing away
Filling and emptying buckets
mechanics.note: Placing water from a bucket

mechanics.name: Falling blocks: sand, gravel, concrete powder, anvils, dripstone, scaffolding
mechanics.note: Sand, red sand, gravel and the concrete powders: when they fall, the falling block's motion, landing, breaking into items, concrete powder in water, and the 100- and 600-tick limits
deviations: concrete powder placed beside water or reached by flowing water does not become concrete
anvils, pointed dripstone, scaffolding and suspicious sand and gravel do not fall
falling blocks hurt nothing

mechanics.name: Wheat growth
mechanics.note: Grows only with light 9 or more at its own cell (minecraft.wiki "Wheat Crops"), light as the tick sees it
deviations: grows with probability 1/3 per random tick, ignoring farmland, hydration and neighboring crops
does not break in darkness and can be placed anywhere

mechanics.name: Other crops and plants: carrots, potatoes, beetroots, stems, sugar cane, cactus, bamboo, kelp, cocoa, berries, nether wart, chorus
Grass, mycelium, nylium, moss and sculk spread
Coral dying without water
deviations: coral blocks and plants (not fans) are inert
water does not flow out of waterlogged fans
mechanics.note: Coral fans and wall fans of every kind die 60 to 99 ticks (a level-random draw) after they are left without water, when placed or updated; they need a sturdy top or face and leave their water when they break; pistons break living fans and move dead ones

mechanics.name: Redstone dust power, shapes and steps
Strong and weak power through solid blocks
mechanics.note: Every state of both versions conducts or not as both official servers report; the rules' answer for blocks with rules of their own matches as well

mechanics.name: Support of components
mechanics.note: Every state's support shape from the registry (collision/support): floor torches and pressure plates on a top whose middle bears them, dust, levers, buttons and wall torches on whole faces

mechanics.name: Redstone torches and burnout
deviations: players place torches on the clicked face, not by their view
floor support comes from collision shapes
no burnout sound or smoke
mechanics.note: Floor and wall torches power every neighbor but their block and the block above them strongly; power in their block turns them off two ticks after an update; the eighth turn-off of a position within 60 ticks burns a torch out for 160 ticks

mechanics.name: Buttons, pressure plates, tripwire and targets
deviations: tripwire is not modeled
no mobs or players press plates yet; only arrows press wooden buttons
of the projectiles only arrows and snowballs hit target blocks
mechanics.note: Buttons of every kind on floors, walls and ceilings: 20 ticks for stone and polished blackstone, 30 for wooden ones, which arrows press and hold; pressure plates of every kind sensing the entities on them (weighted ones counting them); target blocks grading projectile hits

mechanics.name: Daylight detectors, sculk sensors, lightning rods and other sources
deviations: sculk sensors, lightning rods and the other sensors are not modeled
mechanics.note: Daylight detectors, normal and inverted, set their output every 20 game ticks from the sky light in their cell, the time of day, rain and thunder; using one inverts it at once

mechanics.name: Doors, trapdoors, fence gates, note blocks, bells, copper bulbs and other consumers
deviations: bells, copper bulbs and the other consumers are not modeled
copper doors and trapdoors do not weather
player heads with a note block sound of their own play nothing
mechanics.note: Doors, trapdoors and fence gates of every kind open and close with the power around them and by hand (iron ones only by power), quietly, with a level-random draw for the sound; note blocks take the instrument of the block below or a head above and play on a rising signal and when used, as block events that draw for the sound

mechanics.name: Rails, powered, detector and activator rails
deviations: waterlogging is stored only
activator rails act on no minecart (only empty ones exist, which they leave unchanged)
comparators read 0 from detector rails (no minecart has contents)
mechanics.note: Rails take their shapes from the rails beside them and make them join, curve with the official preferences, rise toward higher rails, switch at three-way junctions on updates from signal sources and need a sturdy top; powered and activator rails pass power along up to eight rails of their kind; detector rails sense minecarts, check every 20 ticks and power their ends, neighbors and the block below

mechanics.name: Comparator readings of every container and special block
mechanics.note: Chests and hoppers

mechanics.name: Honey blocks and slime-honey separation
deviations: entities other than items and primed TNT do not slide down honey
mechanics.note: Sticky in piston structures but not to slime; slows what moves on it to 40%; items and primed TNT slide down its sides; moving sideways it carries what stands on it

mechanics.name: Blocks destroyed by pistons and their drops
Moving blocks pushing entities and players
deviations: stuck-entity and piston-base corrections are not modeled
mechanics.note: Entities pushed out of the space a moving block sweeps through each step (0.01 beyond it, at most 0.51 a tick on each axis); moving blocks collide where they stand; moving slime blocks set the speed along their motion to one block a tick; slime blocks bounce what lands on them at 80%

mechanics.name: Push reactions of every block (immovable, destroy, block entities)
mechanics.note: Every block of both versions is moved (pushed and pulled), destroyed, pushed only or left in place as the official servers' pistons treat it; moved blocks arrive without their water

mechanics.name: Dispensers and droppers with dispense behaviors
deviations: dispensed projectiles, fire, bone meal, shears, boats, bottles, honeycomb, glowstone and water bottles at their targets, golem and wither heads, other fluids, other minecarts, spawn eggs, armor stands and shulker boxes are not modeled: those items stay
equipping players is not modeled
water does not flow out of the blocks it waterlogs
mechanics.note: Fired 4 ticks after power reaches them or the block above them, from a random filled slot (level-random draws); droppers fill the container in front or eject; dispensers eject items (position, motion and draws exact), prime TNT, pour and fill water buckets, set minecarts on rails and eject equipment

mechanics.name: Barrels, shulker boxes, ender chests, trapped chests, chiseled bookshelves, composters
Component-aware automation (stacking of items with components)
mechanics.note: Stacks merge only with equal item, damage and components; hoppers, pickups, inserts and menus keep components

mechanics.name: TNT placement and breaking
mechanics.note: TNT placed by commands, pistons and players becomes primed TNT where redstone reaches it; broken, it drops itself by its loot table
deviations: unstable TNT is not primed when broken

mechanics.name: Ignition by redstone, fire, flint and steel, fire charges, burning projectiles and explosions
mechanics.note: Redstone: a signal from any neighbor when TNT is placed, moved in by a piston or updated (blocks, levers, diodes, observers, dust, strongly powered blocks); explosions prime TNT with a fuse of 10 to 29 ticks; a burning arrow primes the TNT it hits; dispensers prime TNT items
deviations: fire, flint and steel (also in dispensers) and fire charges do not ignite TNT yet; of the burning projectiles only arrows are modeled

mechanics.name: Primed TNT entities: fuse, motion, collision and removal
mechanics.note: Creation before the block goes, launch from the level random, the fuse, gravity, collision, ground friction, currents after the move, chunk edges, falling below the world without being removed; it explodes when the fuse runs out and is pushed by other explosions
deviations: lava, bubble columns, portals and entity pushing do not move primed TNT

mechanics.name: Explosions: affected blocks, resistance, fluids, drops, chain reactions, damage and knockback
mechanics.note: TNT's explosion: rays with single-precision intensity and blast resistance (waterlogged blocks resist as water), the reached cells in hash-set order shuffled by the level random, entities hurt and pushed first by distance and exposure (items destroyed or left with less health; nether stars immune; primed TNT pushed from its feet), then blocks cleared with drops merged into stacks of 16, TNT primed with a 10-29 tick fuse, nothing out of the world's height
deviations: entities of one chunk section are hurt in id order, not the order they entered the section
explosions do not hurt or push players yet
a hash-set bucket of eight or more cells (Java turns it into a tree) is ordered as a list

mechanics.name: Live fuses across save, reload and unload
mechanics.note: Fuse, position and motion kept by checkpoints, Anvil and unloading chunks
deviations: after an unload the official servers run a pending tick of the chunk one tick later than Circuit in trace/tnt_reload_pending (their unload timing varies; Circuit unloads dropped chunks at once)

mechanics.name: The tntExplodes game rule
mechanics.note: With the rule off, 1.21.8 does not prime TNT at all; the 1.21.4 harness refuses the skeleton, and 1.21.4 always primes TNT

mechanics.name: Creeper, bed, respawn anchor, end crystal, wither and wind charge explosions
TNT duplication with a named design
deviations: only the Mytteri push duper is established; other designs are untested
reloading its chunk follows the chunk unload timing deviation (open trace tnt_duper_reload)
mechanics.note: The Mytteri push duper primes its TNT on every push after the first while the block moves on, as both official servers do, over eight pushes, in each horizontal direction and across chunk edges and corners, with its documented cobblestone wall (tnt_duper_wall; the earlier traces use stone); restored engines continue it exactly

mechanics.name: Flying machines
deviations: only two-way engine A and the vertical two-way slim engine are established; docks and larger machines are untested
mechanics.note: Two documented engines fly in all six directions with cargo, across chunk edges and into obstacles, as both official servers do

mechanics.name: Gravity-block machines and duplication
deviations: gravity-block duplication needs end portals and is not supported
mechanics.note: Sand and gravel in piston machines (carried by slime, pushed off ledges, dropped by pulled supports, landing on moving pistons) as both official servers do

mechanics.name: Bedrock breaking
mechanics.note: The method documented in text for 1.21 (minecraft.wiki "Tutorial:Breaking bedrock", exploding piston) has a player place a piston while TNT explodes beside them, which needs player-timed placement and explosions that hurt players (C6); the headless-piston method is documented only in videos

mechanics.name: Item sorters, clocks and pulse circuits
mechanics.note: The documented basic hopper item sorter as a whole machine (sorting across a chunk edge, overflow protection); documented pulse generators and limiters; clocks as component cases
deviations: other sorter designs, clocks, pulse extenders and edge detectors are not established as machines

mechanics.name: Typed entities with UUIDs, attributes and components
deviations: the engine models item entities only (more kinds follow in C3.3 and C3.4)
entity UUIDs are derived from ids by the server, not world state (C11)
mechanics.note: Explicit kind, double-precision state, tick count, signed age

mechanics.name: Entity tracking ranges, metadata and visibility for clients
mechanics.note: Items and players

mechanics.name: Entity persistence across save and reload
mechanics.note: Item entities saved with their chunk come back a tick after it reloads, under new ids with new tick counts; checkpoints keep entities waiting to come back
deviations: recovery after a restart keeps ids and tick counts, where an official server loads entities with new ones

mechanics.name: Entity sections, migration between chunks and unloaded chunks
deviations: entities of a reloaded chunk come back in coordinate order, not the official chunk-map order
mechanics.note: Items stop ticking in chunks that are not entity ticking and collide with unloaded cells as with full blocks

mechanics.name: Item entity motion and collision
deviations: moving blocks push items differently (trace/item_piston_push)
entities of a reloaded chunk come back in coordinate order, not the official chunk-map order
mechanics.note: Double-precision gravity, drag, collision with every state's collision boxes, bouncing, the resting rule, currents and buoyancy in water, identical with both official servers in the passing traces

mechanics.name: Item merging
mechanics.note: Every 40 ticks of the item's own count, or every 2 after a move into another block; reach half a block sideways; stacks of one kind within their limit; the smaller joins the larger (equal: the other survives); younger age and longer pickup delay kept

mechanics.name: Pickup by players and hoppers, pickup delays
Despawning
mechanics.note: Age 6000, -32768 never; the age goes up after the item's move and merges

mechanics.name: Arrows, tridents, thrown items, potions, fireworks, wind charges and fishing bobbers
mechanics.note: Arrows and snowballs (summoned): flight, drag in air and water, sticking 0.05 short of the shape they hit, falling again when their block goes, life and despawn, fire counted down and put out by water, burning arrows priming TNT, snowballs breaking on blocks
deviations: projectiles pass through entities
bows, crossbows, dispensers and players do not shoot
currents do not push arrows
tridents, thrown potions, eggs, ender pearls, fireworks, wind charges and fishing bobbers are missing
after an unload the official servers remove a chunk's arrows a tick later than Circuit in trace/arrow_reload (their unload timing varies)

mechanics.name: Boats and rafts
mechanics.note: Empty boats and rafts (summoned): floating with buoyancy, sinking under water, sliding on land with the slipperiness under them, falling, landing on the surface from the air, currents, pushing each other
deviations: a boat floating on still water differs from the official vertical velocity in the last bits after a few ticks (trace/boat_motion; positions stay within 2.2e-16)
riders and paddling
chest boats
bubble columns

mechanics.name: Minecarts of every kind
mechanics.note: Empty minecarts (summoned) off rails — falling, the 0.4 (0.2 in water) speed limit, halving on the ground, 5% drag in the air, water as their last tick ended — and on rails: following the rail's line at up to 0.4 a tick, 4% drag, speeding up down slopes and slowing up them, turning through curves, stopped by blocks, braked by unpowered and boosted by powered powered rails; minecarts collide with each other's and boats' boxes and push each other by their yaw
deviations: a moving minecart picks up the boats it touches (riding is not modeled; it neither picks them up nor pushes them)
yaw from an exact arctangent (the official servers use an approximation; only the push test reads it)
chest, hopper, furnace, TNT, spawner and command block minecarts
riders

mechanics.name: Happy Ghast harnesses and leash changes
Movement checks against block shapes, step-up and corrections
mechanics.note: Walking, jumping and sprinting

mechanics.name: Swimming, crawling, climbing, elytra flight and sleeping
Interaction reach and dig timing
mechanics.note: Reach for blocks and containers; dig time from documented values

mechanics.name: Health, hunger, saturation, exhaustion and regeneration
mechanics.note: Eating is not modeled

mechanics.name: Damage sources and the hurt cooldown
mechanics.note: Falls, the void and starvation

mechanics.name: Death, drops and respawning
deviations: death drops spread in a fixed pattern

mechanics.name: Melee attacks, attack cooldown, critical hits, sweeping and knockback
Placing blocks from items
mechanics.note: 17 item cases, building blocks on both versions (client/building), and every placed state of every block item in fifteen contexts (placement/official_items)

Loot tables for blocks, entities and containers
mechanics.note: Blocks without rules of their own drop from the deterministic subset of their loot tables (913 of 1,007 tables in 1.21.8, 905 of 999 in 1.21.4), with harvest tools and silk touch; modeled blocks keep fixed drops
deviations: tables with random parts (random counts, chances, fortune bonuses, weighted choices) drop nothing until random streams are modeled
tables that copy components or name dynamic contents (shulker boxes, banners, decorated pots) are not used
modeled blocks ignore their tables, so silk touch does not change their drops
entity, container and archaeology tables are not used

mechanics.name: Game rules
mechanics.note: Each bundle lists its game rules with their types and defaults (55 for 1.21.8, 52 for 1.21.4, and the experimental minecartMaxSpeed). Rules are world state: a logged command sets them within the official bounds, checkpoints keep them, and /gamerule queries and sets them with the official replies
deviations: only randomTickSpeed (random ticks) and spawnChunkRadius (the spawn chunks) have behavior; the other rules are kept but change nothing
